title: Proteomics Specialist - Milan (IT) job with Human Technopole | 12865350
gist: Job ad from Human Technopole in Milan for a fixed-term Proteomics Specialist at up to EUR 52,000, supporting high-throughput mass spectrometry proteomics. Skill requirements point to demand for single-cell, spatial, plasma and clinical proteomics at hundreds-to-thousands-of-samples scale.

insights.claim: The Human Technopole Structural Proteomics Unit emphasizes crosslinking MS and high-throughput workflows including single-cell proteomics, and the role targets spatial, plasma and clinical proteomics protocols.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: Hiring shows institutional investment in single-cell, spatial and clinical proteomics.
insights.locator: Join a place where ambitious science thrives

insights.claim: The role involves managing studies of hundreds to thousands of samples, indicating proteomics is being run as a large-cohort, facility-scale operation requiring automation, QC and reproducibility.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: Scale-up and automation demand benefits mass spec and sample-prep tool vendors.

insights.claim: Preferred skills include Astral, Hybrid or Tribrid mass spectrometers, DIA for untargeted proteomics, and machine learning in proteomics data analysis, signaling the instrument and software stack in demand.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: Indicates DIA and Orbitrap-class platforms plus ML analysis are mainstream expectations.

insights.claim: The post is a 3-year contract in Milan paying up to EUR 52,000 with a PhD and at least 5 years of bottom-up proteomics experience required, showing senior skills priced modestly in European academia.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: Low academic pay versus experience may cause talent flow to industry.

insights.claim: Human Technopole offers relocation support and tax benefits for researchers relocating to Italy, suggesting it competes internationally for scarce proteomics talent.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: Retention and recruitment incentives hint at a tight specialist labor market.
